Subject: Aligning partner proof points: storage economics & connector catalog

Hi Samir / Matteo / Evelyn —

Thanks for taking time to collaborate on the storage and vector-store economics story. We want to build a short, repeatable playbook we can present to customers that shows:

- per-query cost delta between hot in-memory indexes vs S3-cold tier fallthrough for typical 10–50k-user apps
- snapshot/restore latency and operational steps for restoring an index from S3-backed cold storage
- expected eviction/KV-cache behavior and how that impacts 95th percentile latency
- recommended SLA language for stores that provide tenant isolation vs shared pools

High-level asks from Redwood: see attached "redwood-storage-econ-ask.pdf" — it contains a two-page benchmarking plan and the data template we need (index sizes, QPS profile, average vector dims).

Internal folks: Marissa and Karthik, we'll want GTM bullets and a co-sell checklist. Ben, can your enablement team produce a concise connector runbook that covers config, observability hooks, and a known-failure play?

Proposed next steps:
1) Partners run the 2-run benchmark in the doc (hot + cold fallthrough) and return the CSV of results;
2) Redwood will run an independent 1-day pass on our infra to validate numbers;
3) Joint one-pager and a short demo for prospects (target: 3 weeks).

Can we schedule a 30-min sync next week? I put a tentative slot on Tuesday — please confirm.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Partnerships
Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood-storage-econ-ask.pdf (PDF, 220KB)
From: Samir Shah <samir@pinecone.io>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 24 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aligning partner proof points: storage economics & connector catalog

Hi Naomi —

Appreciate the clear asks and the template. We'll run the plan but want to flag a few items that affect the numbers:

- Snapshot granularity: are you asking for per-tenant snapshots or multi-tenant full-index snapshots? Per-tenant will add overhead to restore time.
- Cold-tier read amplification: if queries hit S3 directly we see a sharp increase in tail latency; our recommended pattern is a small hot window + async prefetch for predicted queries.
- Cost baseline: are we comparing against a fully-allocated GPU vector index or a sharded CPU-backed pgvector baseline? The delta varies significantly by baseline.

We can deliver a benchmark CSV (index sizes + QPS + 95/99 latencies + egress $) by Thursday. We'll also include a short note on evictions and practical config knobs (ttl, pre-warm windows).

We don't need full infra access from Redwood for the initial pass — a constrained harness running representative requests is sufficient. After we exchange numbers, happy to run a joint validation on Redwood's infra the following week.

I'll attach our internal guide for cold-tier strategies in the follow-up.

—Samir
Samir Shah
Partner Engineering, Pinecone
Attachment: pinecone-cold-tier-notes.pdf (attached in follow-up)

Subject: Re: Aligning partner proof points: storage economics & connector catalog

Great thread — quick GTM notes from my side:

- Audience: prioritize commerce and support-knowledge apps (high read rate, benefit from cold-tiering for historical queries).
- Key customer proof points: 40–60% per-token cost reduction for tail queries + maintained 95th percentile latency under 500ms in our ideal case. We must be conservative in public claims.
- Product collateral: I'll draft a one-pager and co-branded case study template (attached: gtm-onepager.docx).
- Sales enablement: need one demo script that shows failover from hot -> cold and the user-visible impact.

Also, we should plan a partner-facing webinar that focuses on economics and implementation gotchas. Karthik, can you coordinate marketing?

Marissa Cole
Senior GTM, Redwood Inference

Thanks Samir and Marissa — this is helpful. A couple of clarifications from our end:

- Snapshot format: default to full-index snapshots for the benchmark, but please include a short column indicating how results would change for per-tenant snapshots (this helps enterprise customers).
- Baseline: run against our standard GPU-backed Llama-like index baseline (we'll share the exact model dims/seqs in the data template row).
- Cost columns: please include compute $/hour, storage $/GB-month, egress $/GB, and a rough engineering ops effort estimate (low/medium/high).

Ben — can your team turn the "connector-cookbook.md" into an internal enablement stub and a customer-facing quickstart? Attaching the HubSpot pilot record for acme retail: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/98765 (refer to the 'acme-retail-pilot' deal id there). We'll offer a pilot that highlights cold-tier cost savings for infrequently-accessed product history vectors.

Proposed meeting: Tue 26 May 2026 10:30 PT. If that works I'll send a calendar invite and a short agenda.
